fields.explanation: The recovered arXiv 1201.5203v1 PDF supplies the definition omitted from frozen lines 174–175. Its second condition, specialized to two paths P,Q with endpoints u,v, is V(P) ∩ (V(Q) ∖ {u,v}) = ∅; page 4 defines vertex deletion and paths with distinct vertices. Any vertex common to both interiors lies in this intersection, so the condition implies disjoint internal vertex sets. The selected Lean theorem proves that the five-vertex bowtie is connected and bridgeless and has no such pair: every u-to-v walk contains c, which is distinct from both endpoints. Hence every candidate pair violates the printed second condition. This implication is the source-to-certificate argument; the full source predicate is not claimed to be definitionally identical to the Lean predicate. The first printed deletion pair {t,v} is left unchanged and is not needed for the argument. The routes u-c-v and u-a-c-b-v are edge-disjoint but share c internally, so they do not satisfy the recovered vertex condition. The record identifier retains its historical v4 suffix, while the adopted source asset and retrieval receipt identify v1. Frozen missing-definition history is preserved. No refutation of the paper's cycle-double-cover conclusion follows.
fields.flaw: Proposition 2.4 in the recovered arXiv 1201.5203v1 PDF asserts that every pair of distinct vertices in a bridgeless graph has two internally disjoint paths. The second condition in its page-5 definition requires the vertex set of one path to avoid the other path's internal vertices. This implies disjoint internal vertex sets, but the connected bridgeless bowtie has a common internal cut vertex on every path between its two lobes. Thus the auxiliary proposition is false under that printed condition; this does not refute the cycle-double-cover conclusion.

fields.witness: Let V={c,u,a,v,b} and E={{c,u},{u,a},{a,c},{c,v},{v,b},{b,c}}: two triangles sharing only c. Choose distinct vertices u and v. Every edge belongs to a triangle, so deleting any single edge leaves its endpoints connected through the other two triangle edges; hence the connected graph has no bridge. Removing c separates {u,a} from {v,b}, so every path from u to v contains c as an internal vertex. For any two such paths P and Q, c belongs to V(P) ∩ (V(Q) ∖ {u,v}), contradicting the second internally-disjointness condition on page 5 of the recovered arXiv 1201.5203v1 PDF. The selected Lean theorem rules out a pair with disjoint internal vertex sets; the printed source condition implies that property. The frozen extraction's missing formulas remain preserved as historical input.
